## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Random
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Shared random-number helpers
//  - Uniform, normal, and exponential bodies
//  - Gamma- and beta-family bodies
//  - Heavy-tailed, lifetime, and shaped distribution bodies
//  - Discrete distribution bodies
//  - Derived functions for IProbabilityDistribution

library Random
{
    //==
    // # Shared random-number helpers
    //
    // The numerical building blocks every distribution body is written against —
    // factorial, the binomial coefficient, the standard normal density and its
    // rational CDF approximation — plus the `RandomState` hash. The
    // `IProbabilityDistribution` obligations themselves are split by family across
    // the sections below, as is the derived surface built *on top* of the interface
    // (StandardDeviation, SurvivalAt, ProbabilityBetween, ...).
    //
    // ## Special functions
    //
    // The special-function vocabulary lives in `numbers.library.plato`:
    // `Gamma`/`LogGamma`, `Beta`/`LogBeta`, the regularized incomplete forms
    // `RegularizedGammaP`/`RegularizedGammaQ`/`RegularizedBeta`, the error
    // functions `Erf`/`Erfc`, and the modified Bessel functions
    // `BesselI0`/`BesselI1`. The gamma-, beta- and Bessel-dependent distribution
    // bodies (Gamma/Beta/ChiSquared/StudentT Pdf+Cdf, the Weibull moments, the
    // von Mises Variance and Pdf) are implemented against them at their sites.
    // Two deliberate exceptions remain:
    //
    // - VonMises: Cdf has no closed form (an infinite Bessel series) and is
    //   omitted; see its site.
    // - Poisson: Cdf is implemented by direct summation, which is exact-in-form but
    //   O(k); it is not the incomplete-gamma closed form.
    //
    // The normal CDF has no elementary closed form. It predates `Erf` and is
    // computed here with the *named* Zelen & Severo rational approximation
    // (Abramowitz & Stegun 26.2.17), whose stated absolute error bound is 7.5e-8.
    // It is an approximation, not an identity, and is labelled as such at its
    // definition; rewriting it as (1 + Erf(z/sqrt 2))/2 is a separate content
    // change.

    //==
    // # INumerical helpers
    //
    // Small building blocks used by the discrete masses and the normal family.
    // TODO(cross-package): summing an `Array<Number>` is spelled inline as
    // `Reduce(0.0, (total, x) => total + x)` throughout this block; a generic
    // `Sum(IIndexable<Number>)` belongs to the P2 collections package, not here.

    // n factorial (n! = 1*2*...*n) as a Number, with 0! = 1! = 1. Exact for
    // n <= 22 in IEEE double; larger n loses precision and eventually overflows.
    // Precondition: n >= 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Factorial
    Factorial(n: Integer): Number
        => n <= 1
            ? 1.0
            : n.ToNumber * Factorial(n - 1);

    // The binomial coefficient C(n, k), "n choose k", by the multiplicative
    // recurrence C(n, k) = C(n - 1, k - 1) * n / k, which avoids forming the
    // factorials. Precondition: 0 <= k <= n (outside that range the result is
    // meaningless; callers guard the support first).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binomial_coefficient
    BinomialCoefficient(n: Integer, k: Integer): Number
        => k <= 0 || k >= n
            ? 1.0
            : BinomialCoefficient(n - 1, k - 1) * n.ToNumber / k.ToNumber;

    // The density of the standard normal distribution (mean 0, standard
    // deviation 1) at z: exp(-z^2/2) / sqrt(2*pi). Exact.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution
    StandardNormalPdf(z: Number): Number
        => (-0.5 * z.Square).Exp / Number.Tau.Sqrt;

    // The cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution.
    //
    // APPROXIMATION, NOT AN IDENTITY. There is no elementary closed form and
    // this tree declares no error function, so this is the Zelen & Severo
    // rational approximation, Abramowitz & Stegun "Handbook of Mathematical
    // Functions" formula 26.2.17: with t = 1 / (1 + 0.2316419*|z|),
    //   Phi(|z|) = 1 - phi(|z|) * (b1 t + b2 t^2 + b3 t^3 + b4 t^4 + b5 t^5)
    // and Phi(z) = 1 - Phi(-z) for z < 0. The published absolute error bound is
    // |eps| < 7.5e-8, uniformly in z. Do not rely on it beyond ~7 digits, and
    // note that far tail probabilities are accurate in absolute, not relative,
    // terms.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution#Numerical_approximations_for_the_normal_CDF_and_normal_quantile_function
    StandardNormalCdf(z: Number): Number
    {
        var x = z.Abs;
        var t = 1.0 / (1.0 + 0.2316419 * x);
        var poly = t * (0.319381530
                 + t * (-0.356563782
                 + t * (1.781477937
                 + t * (-1.821255978
                 + t * 1.330274429))));
        var upperTail = StandardNormalPdf(x) * poly;
        return z < 0.0 ? upperTail : 1.0 - upperTail;
    }

    //==
    // # RandomState

    // A digest of the generator state. Both fields are part of the value, so
    // they are combined with the classic 31-multiplier mix; Integer arithmetic
    // wraps, which is the intended behaviour for a hash.
    Hash(self: RandomState): Integer
        => self.State.Hash * 31 + self.Stream.Hash;

    //==
    // # Uniform, normal, and exponential bodies
    //
    // The `IProbabilityDistribution` obligations for the four elementary continuous
    // families of `random.types.plato`: UniformDistribution,
    // NormalDistribution, LogNormalDistribution and ExponentialDistribution. Every
    // Pdf and Mean here is exact; the Cdf of the two normal forms inherits the
    // 7.5e-8 error bound of `StandardNormalCdf` in the shared helpers above.

    //==
    // # UniformDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: continuous uniform on the CLOSED interval [Min, Max].
    // Precondition: Min < Max (the degenerate Min == Max case divides by zero).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continuous_uniform_distribution

    // The midpoint of the interval: (Min + Max) / 2.
    Mean(self: UniformDistribution): Number
        => (self.Min + self.Max) / 2.0;

    // The variance of a uniform variable: (Max - Min)^2 / 12.
    Variance(self: UniformDistribution): Number
        => (self.Max - self.Min).Square / 12.0;

    // The density: the constant 1 / (Max - Min) inside [Min, Max], zero outside.
    Pdf(self: UniformDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => value < self.Min || value > self.Max
            ? 0.0
            : 1.0 / (self.Max - self.Min);

    // The cumulative probability: the position of value within the interval,
    // clamped to [0, 1].
    Cdf(self: UniformDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => ((value - self.Min) / (self.Max - self.Min)).Clamp(0.0, 1.0);

    //==
    // # NormalDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: (mean, STANDARD DEVIATION) — the second field is sigma,
    // NOT sigma squared. Precondition: StandardDeviation > 0. `Mean` is already
    // discharged by the field of the same name.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution

    // The variance: the square of the standard deviation.
    Variance(self: NormalDistribution): Number
        => self.StandardDeviation.Square;
```
